nodes.summary: For every $w$ and $b$, the number of examples $k$ with $y_k(x_k^{\mathsf T} w + b) \le 0$ (misclassified or on the decision boundary) is at most the total hinge loss $\sum_k \max(0, 1 - y_k(x_k^{\mathsf T} w + b))$, since each such term is at least $1$.
nodes.title: The hinge loss bounds the number of misclassified examples

nodes.summary: The function $t \mapsto \log(1 + e^t)$ is convex on $\mathbb{R}$, since its derivative, the sigmoid, is nondecreasing. It is the two-term log-sum-exp function $\log(e^0 + e^t)$.
nodes.title: Convexity of the softplus function

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a real $m \times \iota$ design matrix with rows $x_k$, and write $z = X\theta$ for the linear predictor. For any labels $y \in \mathbb{R}^m$, the logistic loss $\theta \mapsto \sum_k \big(\log(1 + e^{z_k}) - y_k z_k\big)$ is convex on $\mathbb{R}^\iota$.
nodes.title: Logistic regression is a convex problem

nodes.summary: For $\lambda \ge 0$, the soft-margin SVM objective $J(w, b) = \sum_k \max(0, 1 - y_k(x_k^{\mathsf T} w + b)) + \lambda\, w^{\mathsf T} w$ is jointly convex in $(w, b)$.
nodes.title: The support vector machine is a convex problem

nodes.summary: For every $t \in \mathbb{R}$, the softplus function $s \mapsto \log(1 + e^s)$ is differentiable at $t$ with derivative the sigmoid $\sigma(t) = 1/(1 + e^{-t}) = e^t/(1 + e^t)$.
nodes.title: Derivative of the softplus function

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a real $m \times \iota$ design matrix with rows $x_k$, and write $z = X\theta$ for the linear predictor. With $p_k = \sigma(z_k) = e^{z_k}/(1 + e^{z_k})$, For labels $y_k \in \{0, 1\}$ the right side is minus the log-likelihood of the observed labels under the logistic model $P(y_k = 1) = p_k$, so minimizing $\ell$ is maximum likelihood estimation.
nodes.title: The logistic loss is the negative log-likelihood of the logistic model

The SVM objective of the affine classifier $x \mapsto x^{\mathsf T} w + b$ is the hinge loss plus a ridge penalty on $w$; the intercept $b$ is not penalized. Eliminating the slack variables of Boyd–Vandenberghe's support vector classifier gives the same hinge terms.
